- Converts saves that the 3.5.x→3.6 converter used to refuse: caches on temporary (FF) actors and leftover global caches are now converted in place.
- Refuses saves that are already converted (for example a later save made from an `_IEconverted` one) instead of double-encoding them.
- Clearer, multi-line output, plus a warning not to load converted saves with any IE 3.5.x.

### Couriers and quests
- Fixed couriers sometimes "arriving" twice, which injected duplicate/blank facts and caused errors after the quest ended.
- Cancelling a quest from the dashboard after the courier arrives now frees the courier properly.
- Courier story facts are recorded when the courier actually arrives, so an aborted courier leaves no facts behind.

### Dashboard hotkey
- Only works while Skyrim is focused, and modifiers must match exactly (a plain 7 no longer fires on Shift+7).
- Changing the hotkey on the SkyrimNet settings page now applies as soon as you click Save, no restart. The dashboard's Settings tab also changes it. Default: Shift+7.

### Other
- Politics settings now persist correctly, and politics can be turned on later without a restart.
- Story DM prompt: knowledge every candidate shares is listed once instead of repeated per NPC.
- Long text is truncated on UTF-8 character boundaries.
- Removed unused internal functions.

This release updates `IntelEngine.dll` and several scripts that must match it; install the whole package over the previous version.

**Antivirus note:** Microsoft Defender may flag the bundled save converter `LegacyCacheMigration.exe` (`Wacapew.C!ml`, a machine-learning heuristic, 1/70 on VirusTotal). It is a false positive and is being reported to Microsoft. The converter is only needed to upgrade 3.5.x saves.

Full changelog: https://github.com/galanx/IntelEngine-GamePlugin/blob/main/CHANGELOG.md#v362
Download: https://github.com/galanx/IntelEngine-GamePlugin/releases/tag/v3.6.2

- Rebuilt the bundled save converter (`LegacyCacheMigration.exe`) so Windows Defender no longer falsely flags it as `Trojan:Win32/Wacatac.B!ml`. 3.6.0 was never harmful; this release just stops the warning.
- No functional changes. `IntelEngine.dll` and `IntelEngine.esp` are identical to 3.6.0, so you can update mid-playthrough without converting your saves again.

- 💾 **Save conversion:** an offline converter (included) repairs saves from earlier versions. **Convert old saves before loading with 3.6.0;** fresh games don't need it.
- **Names kept:** stored NPC names, including names from name mods such as RNE, now survive saves and reloads. Memories and task history no longer corrupt them.
- **Skyrim VR re-enabled:** one shared SE/AE/VR DLL; VR saves from 3.5.1 or earlier can be converted. VR should work (partly tested).
- **Story DM:** stays within the current candidates, leaves disabled story types out of prompts, and skips itself when all eight types are off.
- **NPC Social DM:** safer around save loading.
- **Fixes:** Content Library bio lookup and overlay priority; battle and peace relationship changes now survive reloads; script checks aligned with the native plugin.

Tested on SE/AE 1.6.1170 and 1.7.104 with SkyrimNet Beta 28. 1.5.97 is untested.
Added support for Skyrim SE/AE versions 1.7.x

history.changelog:
Magelight UI 1.6.0 - Nexus changelog

- Gamepad support for pages that opt in (flat only): the d-pad and left stick move between a page's controls, A presses, B goes back or closes the page, and the right stick scrolls.
- While such a page is open the controller belongs to it: no button draws a weapon, attacks, sprints or shouts behind the page, and the B that closes it does not open the Tween menu.
- The button that opened a page does nothing in it until you let go of it.
- Pages that did not opt in, and other mods' own gamepad handling, behave as before.
- Magelight.json: "gamepad": { "enabled": false } turns the gamepad layer off for every page; "glyphs": "playstation" (or "generic") labels the buttons for another controller.
- For mod authors: SetViewGamepad / GetViewGamepadState, the manifest key "gamepad" and the page helper window.magelight.gamepad, with a keys style (no script needed) and a navigation style (focus scopes, tabs, button prompts, an optional stick cursor). Gate on hostVersionNumber >= 10600 or QueryCapability("gamepad"); see CHANGELOG.md and docs/CPP.md.
- Thanks to ColdSun for the gamepad layer.

## Magelight UI 1.5.1

A small fix release on top of 1.5.0, all about the mouse cursor:

- **Crash fix:** mods that read the game's cursor every frame could crash the game alongside Magelight, often as a chat page opened. Fixed.
- **Menus over pages:** opening a context or item menu over a page no longer rebuilds the game's cursor.
- **Cursor stays in the game:** while a page has the mouse, the Windows cursor can no longer wander onto another monitor.

Both cursor changes are flat-screen only and can be turned off in `Magelight.json` (`"pinGameCursor": false`, `"clipCursor": false`). VR is unchanged.

Magelight UI 1.5.0

Magelight now runs on Ultralight 2.0, the newest version of the web engine behind every Magelight page. Pages look the same, run a little lighter, and a long list of fixes comes with it.

Highlights
- Japanese, Chinese and Korean typing: the IME's candidate list now shows inside the page, so you no longer pick characters blind. It matches the text field's font and the page's colours. (Thanks to Dekana, who built and tested this.)
- Escape while typing with an IME only closes the candidate list or clears the word you're typing. It no longer closes the chat and loses your text. With Korean, one Escape commits the syllable and closes, as in Windows.
- Fixed a crash and an "overlay disabled" problem for players using CrashLogger 1.23 or newer: an error in any mod's page could take down the UI or the game. Pages now run on their own stack and errors stay inside the page.
- Opening a page no longer makes your character sheathe their weapon or drop a readied spell.
- HUD-style views (widgets that don't take clicks) now show during play with ENB, ReShade and other graphics wrappers.
- Opening and closing pages no longer rebuilds the game's cursor, which could crash some cursor mods. The Journal and Inventory keep their cursor too.
- Alt-tabbing no longer fills Magelight.log with false "stall" reports.

Smaller improvements
- Pages that load in the background open with their images already drawn.
- Memory used by hidden pages is given back on its own, even when no page is open.
- Mouse: drags end where you release, the mouse wheel scrolls what's under the pointer, middle-click no longer autoscrolls, and the back/forward mouse buttons work in pages.
- VR: the keyboard follows the text field you're typing in, shows a number pad or email/URL layout where it fits, and has Undo, Redo, Cut, Copy and Paste buttons. Each hand drags and points on its own.
- Japanese fonts like MS UI Gothic and MS PGothic draw in the right face again.

history.changelog:
## Improvements

- **Set me up:** Checks your graphics card and your game, shows which models fit alongside Skyrim, and installs the ones you tick.
- **Add a PC:** Open one address on a spare PC and it pairs itself. No pairing codes to type.
- **One list of every model:** The new **Models** tab shows every model on all your PCs. You can start, stop, remove, or delete them from there.
- **A guard for your game:** If your graphics memory gets too full while Skyrim is running, MultiProxy stops its local chat model to prevent a crash.
- **Works on Skyrim VR:** One mod file now covers Skyrim SE, AE, and VR, and it no longer needs Address Library.
- **and a lot more:** See the full release notes on Github.

**Your gaming PC and your spare computers can now team up to run the AI together.**

* **Local models:** Pick a model, hit download, and MultiProxy runs it on your graphics card for free while leaving enough memory for Skyrim.
* **The Courier:** Run a small app on a spare PC or laptop to use its models from your gaming rig. It updates itself, and if a device drops offline, MultiProxy moves on to your next choice.
* **Quick decisions:** A fast, private model handles SkyrimNet's constant stream of background questions on any of your PCs.
* **Voice and speech:** NPCs speak using voices generated on your own hardware, and you can reply using push-to-talk (speech to text through xAI, off until you turn it on).
* **Routing:** Choose which model handles each job—like Dialogue, Combat, and Memory—and set up your backups.
* **New providers:** Grok, Continuum, Cloudflare Workers AI, Mistral, and Groq.
* **One installer:** It brings your old settings along, includes the Skyrim mod, and puts an icon by your clock.

- **Ready for SkyrimNet Beta 25:** Beta 25 can swap to a backup AI if your primary stalls, or race a second request against a slow one. MultiProxy reports real failures immediately so handoffs trigger cleanly instead of an NPC reading error code out loud! Canceled race requests are cleared away without cluttering your Speeds tab.
- **Voice cues left alone:** Beta 25 uses distinct tags per voice engine, so cues pass through untouched by default. If you use Higgs, toggle `FixHiggsVoiceTags` to keep them clean.
- **Tougher under pressure:** Courtesy of community member Raydonn, dropped connections retry automatically, long chats trim and retry instead of going silent, and scrambled markup tags get repaired before SkyrimNet sees them.
- **Waiting lines:** Also from Raydonn, cap simultaneous requests per provider (`[Concurrency]` in `proxy.ini`) to dodge rate limits. GLM defaults to 6.
- **Full reply log:** Turn on `LogFullReplies` to print complete AI replies directly in your console.
- **Smarter Speeds tab:** Live health cards for each AI, tracking how fast replies start talking, overall speeds, and plain reliability labels, with Dialogue front and center.

**Fixes**
- **Mod Organizer 2:** The Speeds tab reliably finds SkyrimNet folders on MO2 setups.
- **Faster DeepSeek:** Skips the hidden "thinking" step by default, matching GLM.
- **Privacy:** The Speeds tab no longer enables SkyrimNet stats sharing; manage that directly in SkyrimNet's Privacy settings.

plugins.title: ModPacer

history.changelog:
### What's New

- **Sort your mods:** pick **Default order**, **Name A to Z** or **Name Z to A** above your list, and ModPacer remembers your choice.
- **Set missing versions:** if **Vortex** doesn't know a mod's version, click the new "It's <version>" button so we can check for future updates.
- **One options screen per update:** you now make your mod choices just once, even if **Vortex** is busy.
- **Clearer logs:** the update log now shows every step of an options-screen installation so you can easily track what happened.

### What's New v1.1.9

- **Vortex updates:** ModPacer only removes the old version after checking that the new one is installed and switched on. If the new one is missing, your old mod is not removed.
- **Waiting for a busy Vortex:** Clicking **Update** on a single mod now waits patiently if Vortex is slow to answer, instead of reporting a failed removal.
- **Vortex Updates:** Update all now waits for a busy Vortex and removes the old versions it replaced. Any old versions left behind are removed too, or listed with a Remove old versions button.
- **Tidier Add-on List:** Add-ons whose files are missing no longer appear as blank rows, and add-ons not found on the Hub now display their names.

### What's New

- **Hand-Updated Add-ons:** Add-ons you manually update in Mod Organizer 2 now show their true version and no longer prompt for unneeded updates.
- **Better Version Checks:** ModPacer now correctly compares four-part and beta version numbers, so real updates are no longer missed.
- **Clearer Logs:** The update log now tracks every download from start to finish, recording the exact version found and where it came from.

### What's New

- **Exclude a Mod:** Click Exclude in Mods not installed to stop listing and downloading a mod, and use Settings to view Excluded mods or click Include again.
- **Better Mod Organizer 2 Detection:** ModPacer now judges each add-on by its own files, so similar-looking folders no longer count as installed and old versions stop showing false updates.

### What's New

- **Nexus Details in Vortex:** Mods installed from Nexus now carry their details into Vortex, so the "missing identification information" warning no longer appears.
- **Smoother Updates:** Update all installs every new mod first, then removes the old ones together under "Removing old mods", without "Mod not found" warnings.
- **Cleaner Startup:** ModPacer opens just one Mods section, says so if it is already running, and the installer closes running copies first.

### What's New

- **Broader MO2 Detection:** Detects SkyrimNet in Mod Organizer 2's Overwrite and Stock Game folders to support custom modlists like Nolvus and Nordic Souls.
- **Respects MO2 Load Order:** Reads the winning copy of SkyrimNet when multiple exist, and alerts you if the only installed copy is disabled.
- **Improved Add-on Tracking:** Recognizes add-ons as installed whether they are located in the Overwrite folder or any active mod.
- **Flexible Folder Recognition:** Correctly identifies installed MO2 mods even if their folder names differ from their official listing names.
- **Self-Exclusion Fix:** ModPacer no longer incorrectly lists itself under "Mods not installed."
- **Streamlined Alerts:** Provides shorter, clearer messages when SkyrimNet is missing or an add-on hasn't registered.
- **Interactive Setup Fallback:** Prompts you to manually select the SkyrimNet folder during setup if auto-detection fails, rather than halting the installation.
- **True Clean Uninstall:** Choosing "Delete settings" during uninstallation now completely removes all ModPacer traces.

**What's New**

- **Fixed SkyrimNet Folder Detection:** Resolved an issue where ModPacer could mistakenly select a subfolder created by an add-on instead of the main SkyrimNet directory, resulting in a Could not read content-registry.json error. 

- **Improved Logging:** Setup and installation errors are now accurately captured in the diagnostic log, making troubleshooting and support requests much easier.

**Mod Organizer 2** users: this update is for you. 

- Mod Organizer 2 and Wabbajack modlists are now properly handled.
- Mod Organizer 2: can now pick your Mod Organizer 2 folder and ModPacer finds your mods and Skyrim folder from it.
- Added logging, which is on by default, but can be turned off in settings.
- Tells you when a newer ModPacer is out.
Initial Release

# SeverActions 4.6.0 - Blood and Thread

**Bundled with it:**
- **Magelight UI 1.5.1:** Ultralight 2.0, less memory after pages close, in-page IME typing, crash fixes, pages no longer put your weapons away, and the cursor stays in the game window.
- **Phantasm:** a separate renderer that now draws the Outfits mirror, the Inventory item view and the party's faces. It installs with SeverActions.(Will be it's own separate mod with an API to hook into in the future)

If you also run Magelight UI as its own mod, let the newer copy win.

## :drop_of_blood: Survivable dismemberment (highly experimental)
Needs Dismembering Framework. Off until you turn it on (Settings → Combat Context, or the MCM's Combat & Outlaws page).
- A power attack with a sword or axe that leaves someone at low health can take a forearm or lower leg **without killing them**. They stagger, scream and beg for the fight to stop.
- Most surrender after losing an arm. A brave fighter (a boss, or at least your level) keeps fighting with the other hand (not in VR).
- A lost leg, or both hands, knocks them down for good.
- **The wound bleeds** until they die. Adept-or-better Restoration healing (Heal Other, Grand Healing) from you or a follower closes it.
- They remember who cut them, and who they surrendered to.
- Followers, guards, children and essential characters are never cut.
- Limbs don't grow back yet; that's coming in a later update, alongside possible prosthetics.

-See Announcement Page For More

## **SeverActions v4.5.0** — Mirrors and Motives

A new Outfits page built around a live mirror, a reworked Inventory with trading, a way to see why your companions feel the way they do, NPCs who can study spell tomes, and NPCs who level up with you.

SeverActions v4.3.0 — Law and Language
A Law & Crime page, guards who stop to talk before they arrest your companions, a language setting with full translations, situation outfits for you, and Bio Blocks starter packs with a bigger API.
- See announcement page for more information

## **SeverActions v4.2.0** — Colours and Clarity
- See announcement channel for the full changelog

Colour themes, presets that stay on, real control over a follower's built-in spells, a bigger quick wheel, plainer menus and a corrected Russian translation.

:warning: **Before you update**
- **Replace over 4.1.x** in MO2. The installer's pages and choices are the same, and saves carry over.
- **FOMOD Plus users:** the installer now always installs the module scripts, so installs that came out missing scripts get all of them.
- **Magelight UI 0.31.2 is included.** If you also run it as its own mod, let the newer copy win.

:art: **Themes**
- **Five themes** in Settings > UI Display: The Ledger (today's look), Windhelm Slate, Dwemer Verdigris, Soul Cairn and Jarl's Vellum, a light theme.
- **Everywhere:** every page, popup and the quick wheel, and the cursor takes the theme's colours too.

:dress: **Outfits**
- **Presets stay on** after fast travel, sleep and waiting, and a sleep outfit no longer dresses a follower over a preset.(needs further testing)
- **Situation outfits** No timer on situation switches
- **Inventory** lists armour freed from a default outfit again, with a Take off button for worn pieces.
- **Warmth:** 100% means a full set of warm gear, so ordinary armour no longer reads "Bare".

:magic_wand: **Spells**
- **Turn off built-in spells:** switching off a spell on the Spells page really stops a follower casting it, including ones they came with. Built-in spells are marked, and ones shared by other NPCs say why they can't be removed.

:joystick: **Quick wheel and hotkeys**
- **Twelve slots,** showing only the ones you fill.
- **Key capture always ends,** and VR warns when the menu chord clashes with another binding.

:moneybag: **Enterprises and off-screen life**
- **Work marks are back:**

## SeverActions 4.1.0
Magelight UI 0.30.5 is included in the SeverActions download and is also available on its own.

**SeverActions 4.1.0**
- **Wait and Follow work on the first press.** Wait All and Follow All finish in a second or two instead of seeming to do nothing. Each command now undoes only what SeverActions actually put on a follower, which helps custom followers most.
- **Faster loading.** On a long-running save, SeverActions' startup after a load went from about a minute to about 12 seconds, and commands given right after a load no longer wait 20+ seconds.
- Companions are no longer pushed back onto their follow package every few seconds.
- Mouse and gamepad buttons (M3, M4, M5…) work again as the menu and quick wheel keys, and Settings > Hotkeys can capture them.
- Tracking mode: casual follow works again for NPCs no follower framework leads.
- The Companions page now shows the framework mode the game is actually using.
- If Magelight can't draw, the menu and wheel keys now tell you so (and point to Magelight.log) instead of doing nothing.
- Outfits mirror on CPU rendering: the Live Stage takes over instead of leaving a hole in the menu. In VR it's a dark box.

**Magelight UI 0.30.5** (includes 0.30.4)
- Menus no longer open invisible with DLSS or frame generation behind NVIDIA Streamline (Community Shaders, Open Shaders).
- Community Shaders frame generation: the UI shows again.
- NVIDIA Smooth Motion: opening a menu no longer freezes the game.
- A lost graphics device turns the overlay off instead of leaving the game paused.
- A new, sharper cursor, and no more double cursor.

**Installing:** install over 4.0.x with Replace. Saves load as they are. Still needs SkyrimNet 0.25 or newer.

## SeverActions 4.0.2 — Hotfix

Updates the bundled **Magelight UI to 0.30.3**, which fixes three problems in 4.0.1:

**Fixed: crash at startup with Community Shaders**, or a few minutes into play with ENB or an upscaler (`d3d11.dll` in the crash log)
**Fixed: crash at startup with ENB** that left no crash log
**Fixed: menu cut off** on screens under ~1067 pixels tall (1366×768, 1600×900)

If you made a `Magelight.json` to work around the ENB crash, you can delete it now.

**Installing:** install over 4.0.1 and choose **Replace**. Your saves load as they are.

history.changelog:
NPCs now scheme against each other in the background, and visits handle you leaving.

## What's New

### NPC Plots

- Unique NPCs pursue schemes of their own, planned as concrete steps (theft, bribery, rumors, denunciation, blackmail, sabotage, forgery, crafting and more) that run over in-game days.
- Schemers send people they can command; a step's odds depend on who does it and to whom, preparing makes it easier, and a failed step means another way or giving up.
- Plots leave memories in SkyrimNet: schemers, agents, targets and officials all remember their part.
- Schemers and agents know about their plot in conversation, and keep it secret.

> **Note:** Plots need a decision provider set up in SkyrimNet.

> **Note:** Plots are a background simulation for now and won't be reflected in an NPC's native in-game behavior. This will be revisited in a future release.

### The Dashboard

- A new Plots tab shows every plot, its steps, odds and outcomes, with a Simulation Enabled checkbox.

> **Important:** Requires SkyrimNet Beta 26 (0.26.0) or newer.

> **Important:** Running IntelEngine alongside is not recommended; if you do, turn its Story Engine off.

> **Important:** Don't modify NarrativeEngine's prompts for non-English output; it can disrupt the simulations.

## Fixes

- Ghosts no longer take part in gossip or plots, or write letters and visit.
- A visit is called off if you go somewhere it could never start before the visitor greets you.
- Fast-travelling away ends a visit; mid-conversation, the visitor remembers you left abruptly.

The Director could start a letter, visit or ambush using something it was never offered, so a hallucinated NPC could show up at your door. Every pick is now checked against the options offered for that specific beat. An invalid pick gets one retry; if that also fails, nothing fires until the next evaluation.

## Fixes

- A visit or letter could come from an NPC who was never a valid sender for it, for example a leveled guard, your current follower, or someone who was only eligible to write a letter. That happened when the Director named an NPC that wasn't on the list. Senders are now checked against the list offered for that exact beat.
- A letter or visit could go ahead without its intended topic when the Director named a memory the sender didn't have. The composer then quietly picked a topic itself. That pick is now rejected.
- An ambush that named an attacker group nobody had offered quietly fell back to the first eligible group. That pick is now rejected.

A pacing and placement update: visits stop arriving back to back, beats repeat less often, and beats no longer fire in other realms or sealed-off places.

## What's New

### Visits

- After any NPC visit, no other visit can happen for 24 in-game hours. Until now only the same visitor was held back, so different NPCs could turn up one after another.
- The new `iVisitBeatCooldownGameHours` setting in `NarrativeEngine.ini` controls how long the pause lasts. Set it to 0 to turn the pause off.
- A visit that's called off before the visitor reaches you doesn't start the cooldown.

> **Note:** Existing saves load normally. On the first load of an older save the cooldown starts clear, so the next visit isn't held back.

### The Director

- The Director now waits 15 minutes before choosing the same kind of beat again, up from 5. The old window mostly ran out while the beat was still playing, so it rarely prevented a repeat.

## Fixes

- Beats no longer fire in places nobody could plausibly reach you. Previously Vigilants of Stendarr could ambush you in the Soul Cairn. The default location blacklist now covers the Soul Cairn and the Boneyard, Apocrypha, the Mind of Pelagius, the inside of Azura's Star, the Forgotten Vale, Darkfall Passage, Ancestor Glade, the Throat of the World summit and path, Giant's Grove, Japhet's Folly, Brinewater Grotto, Forebears' Holdout and all of Castle Volkihar. It also still covers Sovngarde. Fort Dawnguard is deliberately left off.

A small workaround for a rare case where Skyrim's own courier stops making deliveries.

## Fixes

- If Skyrim's pending-delivery counter has been driven below zero by something outside NarrativeEngine, the vanilla courier stops being dispatched and letters sit undelivered. The plugin now raises that counter to match the letters actually waiting whenever it stages one.

Visiting NPCs now walk Skyrim's real roads and arrive under cover, and the bug behind the "gossip isn't spreading" reports is fixed.

## What's New

### NPC Visits

- Visitors travel Skyrim's actual road network instead of a straight line from home; both road graphs ship enabled.
- The arrival spot is found by walking out along their route to the first place far enough off and out of sight.
- Cover is preferred outright over open ground, so a visitor appears behind a rock at 6,000 units rather than in the open at 5,000.
- Visitors can finally arrive inside walled cities like Whiterun and Windhelm.
- Minimum arrival distance rises from 800 to 2,000 units, so nobody appears across the road from you.
- A stuck visitor can hop along the road around an obstacle before walking the long way round.

## Fixes

- Gossip could stop spreading: rumors surviving a save came back unable to advance, yet held live-rumor slots until the cap filled and the world stopped seeding.
- Letters and visits could reference things the sender had no way of knowing; the Director now names one of the sender's own memories.
- With you upstairs in an inn, a visitor could be sent to a balcony door instead of the street-level front door.
- Which door a visitor waited at was a coin flip in 279 of 544 vanilla interiors; now it is the same door every time.
- A visitor could arrive thousands of units off their own route, or almost on top of you inside a city gate.

> **SkyrimNet Beta 25 (0.25.0) or newer is now required.** This release ships only the new plugin layout; on Beta 24 or earlier SkyrimNet finds none of NarrativeEngine's prompts and every LLM-driven beat fails. Update SkyrimNet, or stay on v0.6.1. Let your mod manager replace the whole mod rather than merge into it.

Full release notes: https://github.com/pdusen/skyrimnet-plugin-narrative-engine/releases/tag/v0.7.0

# NarrativeEngine v0.6.1

Walled-city visitors now reach you and greet you indoors, letter and visit prompts see only what the two of you said to each other, and every dashboard tab says when its next thing happens.

## What's New

### The Dashboard

- Every tab with a cadence now shows when the next thing happens: Director evaluations, dispatch cooldowns, the gossip schedule, letter delivery, and the visit approach, return-home and poll deadlines.
- Each readout is labelled with the clock that governs it — real, unpaused, active play, or game time — because those four elapse at different rates.
- A cooldown that is switched off reads as an em dash rather than 0s.

> **Note:** The numbers do not tick while you watch. Opening the dashboard pauses the game, freezing three of the four clocks.

### Beat Senders

- New `sBlacklistedSenders` under `[Beats]` names NPCs who may never write you a letter or pay you a visit. Semicolon-separated, matched on editor ID or in-game name.

> **Note:** Read at load, so a change needs a restart. Editor-ID matching needs an editor-ID recovery mod (powerofthree's Tweaks); without one use the in-game name.

### Letters and Visits

- The dialogue history behind a letter or visit is now strictly what passed between you and that NPC. Third-party lines and ambient chatter are dropped.

### Ambushes

- The narration logged when an ambush begins no longer contains speech of any kind. The attackers do their own talking.

## Fixes

- An NPC living inside a walled city will now travel to you when you are nowhere near it. Previously most visits from Whiterun, Riften, Solitude, Markarth and Windhelm residents never happened at all.
- A visitor who follows you indoors now greets you, instead of trailing you until the approach timed out.

Full release notes: https://github.com/pdusen/skyrimnet-plugin-narrative-engine/releases/tag/v0.6.1

## What's New

### NPC Visits

- Visitors arrive from along the road between the player and the sender's home, not on a bearing unrelated to how they would have travelled.
- A visitor whose home lies outside a walled city walks in through that city's gate — the nearest one to the player when there are several.
- When the player is indoors, the visitor is placed on the far side of the player's own door and comes in through it.
- Senders who are not loaded — almost all of them — are now located from their save cell or their location's map marker.
- The arrival band widened from 2500 to 5000 units and the approach timeout from 60 to 90 seconds; the old ceiling discarded ~70% of the road on a route.
- The cover check sweeps a whole visitor's height rather than stopping at the chest, and open ground outside the player's view arc is accepted when there is no cover.

> **Note:** Past roughly 2000 units an arrival can ride a cover claim the raycast cannot support, so a visitor may occasionally appear in plain sight.

### Debug Notifications

- Optional corner-of-screen notices when a beat does something unseen: a visitor warped in, a letter given to the courier, an ambush spawned, a rumor seeded. Off by default; a testing aid, not a gameplay feature.

### SkyrimNet Beta 25

- Content ships in Beta 25's plugin layout alongside the old one, so either version works.

## Fixes

- The dashboard hotkey matched mouse buttons as well as keys, so scrolling could open or close it.
- A null field in an event payload threw away the whole batch after it.
- Log rotation renamed the current file, detaching any editor tailing it; it copies now.
- The courier's cached lookup was not cleared on save load.
- The MCM event sink traced every other mod's events.

Full release notes: https://github.com/pdusen/skyrimnet-plugin-narrative-engine/releases/tag/v0.6.0

history.changelog:
Fixes for 1.1.0's bio blocks.

## 🐛 Fixed
- 🧩 **NPCs who already carry blocks no longer get new rolls.** The Blocks column kept rolling the groups such an NPC had left empty, and since rolls are fresh each launch, every session offered them a few more traits. An NPC with blocks applied to them (by you, or by an earlier commit) is now done: only a fact can still fill a gap. Blocks granted by a SeverActions faction rule don't count.
- 🔎 **The review keeps rolls more faithfully.** The model was replacing a roll whenever the evidence supported a *different* option in the same group: a chief with two wives lost Exhibitionism to Polygamy, "suspicious of outsiders" replaced Cruel, a trained warrior lost "dislikes violence". It's now told that evidence for another option isn't evidence against the roll, and to replace only when the two can't both be true.
- 🧾 **Review answers are read more reliably.** Answers written as `keep - it fits`, or with the format's `(reason)` placeholder copied in, are now read correctly, and the prompt shows real quoted examples instead of a placeholder.

Adds SeverActions bio blocks: short traits like a religion, a phobia or a vice, given to NPCs alongside their bios.

## ✨ New
- 🧩 **Bio blocks** ([SeverActions](https://github.com/Severause/SeverActions) Bio Blocks API v4). With SeverActions installed, BioForge gives each NPC a few of SeverActions' bio blocks when their bio is committed. Blocks are separate from the bio: they show beside it, and the bio itself is never changed.
- 📜 **Facts from game data.** A Vigilant of Stendarr worships Stendarr, a Stormcloak dislikes the Empire, a drunk sounds like one. Facts are fixed and never second-guessed.
- 🎲 **Flavour is rolled, then checked.** Each trait group (religion, temperament, dislikes, phobias, vices...) rolls on its own chance, for variety. A model then reviews the rolls against the NPC's evidence: it keeps a roll unless the evidence contradicts it, and adds one only where the evidence names it outright. Every change carries a quoted reason, and a change with none is ignored. For a new bio the review rides the same generation, with no extra call; the bio is written to match.
- 🔍 **Review blocks** for NPCs who already have a bio: one small LLM call per NPC (row or batch), staged for you to read before anything is applied. The existing bio is never touched.
- 📋 **The reader shows a blocks table**: each block's verdict (fact, kept, changed, added, dropped), and the model's reason.
- 🔁 **Reroll** in the Blocks column rolls an NPC's flavour again. Rolls are fresh each game launch and hold for the session.
- 🎭 **Anything can happen, rarely.** Every block is reachable; rare sets share a fixed pool (any Daedric Prince: about 1 NPC in 40), so the odd secret Daedra worshipper turns up without crowding the rest.
- ✏️ The rules live in `SKSE/Plugins/BioForge/block_rules.ini`, a commented text file you can edit.

## 🛠️ Changes
- 🪟 BioForge's popups are fully opaque, so the panel no longer shows through the text.

Adds the option to run BioForge on its own LLM.

## ✨ New
- 🧠 **A separate model for BioForge** ([#4](https://github.com/Oldcustard/BioForge/issues/4)). BioForge now adds a `bioforge` model to SkyrimNet's LLM settings, and a new setting, **Use BioForge's Own LLM**, switches bios, the relationship refine pass and regional digests over to it. It's **off by default**: BioForge keeps using your Character Profile Generation model, exactly as before.

## ⚠️ Before you turn it on
Set up the `bioforge` model in SkyrimNet's LLM settings first, and raise its **max tokens to about 10,000**. Until it's configured it inherits SkyrimNet's dialogue defaults (4,096 tokens), which cut bios short and make them fail with missing sections.

Bug-fix release for non-English installs and creature scanning.

## 🐛 Fixes
- 🌍 **NPCs with non-English names are detected correctly** ([#1](https://github.com/Oldcustard/BioForge/issues/1)). Bios for NPCs with Cyrillic (or any non-ASCII) names were never matched to their file, so those NPCs kept showing as needing a bio even when one existed.
- 🏘️ **Regional digests handle non-English names**: those characters are now ranked properly instead of sinking to the bottom, and settlements with non-English names no longer share one cached digest.
- 🐴 **Creatures are no longer scanned.** Named horses such as Shadowmere or a mod's stable horses were being offered bios; anything whose race isn't a person's is now skipped.

history.changelog:
**Improvements**
- Someone caught in a fight without fighting (a farmer, a passing townsman) is no longer mentioned at all, so your followers stop deciding you're a murderer. Want them back? "Mention bystanders who were killed" on SkyrimNet's settings page.
- Enemies killed before they noticed you still count. Stealth archers rejoice!
- Your summons and your followers' (Scrap, a conjured skeleton, a spectral wolf, a raised corpse) are no longer fighters of their own, and nobody mourns them. Their kills are their master's: "Remiel 3 (Wolf x3, 2 through Scrap)".
- The enemy's summons are told as dispatched, with credit: "Summoned creatures dispatched: Lydia 1 (Flame Atronach)". Any that disappear with their master's death count for nobody.
- Several enemies with the same name are numbered: "the first Troll", "the second Troll", so it's clear which one struck your follower down.
- Follower Death and Injury Chance is now officially supported: a minor, a serious or a lasting injury.

**Bug Fixes**
- "Ignore friendly fire" now also covers bystanders caught in the crossfire. Thanks to Zol for the change.
- Effects that did no damage (an aura pulsing over everyone nearby) are no longer blamed on anyone. Thanks to Zol.
- Two creatures that the game gave the same ID to are no longer mixed up.

**Support for Custom Wording**
- Every phrase the mod writes can now be reworded: about 150 of them, from "took solid wounds" to "burned by fire".
  Want it darker, stricter, or just different? See "Your own wording" in the README.
- Could be useful for translations.

**Bug Fixes and Enhancements**
- Someone killed without fighting is no longer called "an innocent". The summary says they were "not actively engaged
  in combat" and leaves the rest to the story. Thanks to nan0bug00 for the change.
- An enemy cut down before he could draw his sword no longer counts as someone who wasn't fighting.
- When the mod can't tell what hurt someone, it says so plainly: a wolf's bite is no longer "harmful magic".
- A spell, potion or weapon is only named when the attacker actually used it. No more odd internal names.
- Multiple actors with the same name doing the same thing are told once, not three times (example: 3 wolves
  attacking you).

**Friendly fire**
- Caught your follower in a fireball? It's now told as an accident, not as an attack on them.
- Or switch it off entirely and they'll stop bringing it up. (A death by friendly fire is always told.)

**Settings in SkyrimNet**
- Battle Summaries now has its own page in SkyrimNet's settings, under Plugins. The ini still works.

**Moments**
- Several enemies killed in one stroke get a mention, with what did it: "killed 3 at once with Fireball".

**Fixes**
- An enemy who happens to kill another enemy no longer "saves" your follower's life.
- Damage done to your own side no longer counts as doing the fighting.
- "Killed by someone" is gone.

- **Injuries from injury mods.** A fighter who picks up an injury during the battle is told so ("was injured in this fight and still carries it: Leg Injury"), and one they already had is told as brought into the fight. Works with Blade and Blunt and Wildcat; any other injury mod that marks its injuries with a keyword can be added in the ini (`[OtherMods] sInjuryKeywords`).
- **Beheadings and severed limbs.** Told with the kill ("Lydia beheaded Bandit Chief."): Dismembering Framework for limbs, Next-Gen Decapitations for heads, and the game's own beheadings. None of these mods is required.
- **Innocents and allies slain.** A citizen or guard cut down without ever raising a weapon is told as an innocent, with who killed them, and is no longer counted among the enemies. An ally killed by their own side is told as that.
- **How long the battle lasted** is told as a figure ("It lasted 42 seconds.", "It lasted about 25 minutes.").
- **A battle ends with its enemies.** It no longer stays "underway" for as long as the game keeps the party in combat with wildlife that never fought, and time spent in menus is not counted in its length.
- **Kill credit.** The game names the player for some deaths the player had no part in; a kill now goes to the player only when the player struck the victim.

Injuries and dismemberment can be switched off in `BattleSummaries.ini` (`bInjuries`, `bDismemberment`). Replace the old version when updating; do not merge into it.
Initial release

plugins.tagline: Build relationships naturally and organically in a world where every character is unique
plugins.author: deadohiosky

history.changelog:
**They remember where they stand with you, every time.** Sometimes a close friend or a spouse talked to you like a stranger for no reason. That's fixed. How they feel about you is there in every conversation now, even the first one after you load.

**Old friends aren't strangers.** If you've known someone for months, they won't be treated like someone you met yesterday. And for a history that started before Relationships was installed, open their card and write it under Your history with them: "Beirand and I have been friends since his apprenticeship in Hammerfell." They'll take it as fact, and they'll remember it when you talk.

**Two new Bond Pace settings.** Very Slow for a romance that takes the whole playthrough, Very Fast if you play at a low timescale and want things to move.

**What they call you sticks only when it was actually said.** No more pet names pulled from months-old memories, or garbled ones. Tell someone "call me Handsome" and it sticks, even in an otherwise quiet chat. If a name's wrong, Forget what they call you on their card clears it, and they'll stop using it.

**Re-author can start their bio blocks over**, including ones you picked, if you tick the new box.

Characters stay warm and affectionate while they're not ready for more, and nobody sparks a romance minutes after meeting you.

Install over 2.3.x with Replace, DLL included; saves carry over. Requires SkyrimNet Beta 25 or newer, SKSE and Address Library. For the dashboard: Meridian UI 1.5.0+, Magelight UI 0.30.5+ or Prisma UI 1.5.1+.

**Relationships speaks your language.** Pick one under Language in the mod's settings, or leave it on Game to follow Skyrim's. The dashboard, the notices, the question and your answer to it are all in that language. So is everything written for you to read: why someone feels as they do, the line they won't cross, what just happened between you.

**Eighteen languages.** English, Arabic, Chinese, Czech, Dutch, French, German, Hebrew, Hindi, Hungarian, Italian, Japanese, Korean, Polish, Portuguese, Russian, Spanish and Turkish. In Arabic and Hebrew the dashboard reads right to left.

**The bio blocks come along.** The blocks Relationships gives characters in SeverActions are written in your language too.

**These are first drafts.** Every language but English was translated by machine and hasn't been read by a native speaker yet. If something reads wrong, tell us; each language is one file, and fixes are quick. In some scripts, Skyrim's own notice font may show boxes where the dashboard shows the words.

Characters already written keep their wording until they're re-authored.

**HOTFIX - No more Landmarks out of nowhere.** Since 2.2, people nearby get judged when something big happens. If one of them hadn't said a word to you, the judge could still read her diary (which may have been last written to weeks ago), see that she wanted a life with you, and call it a Landmark: the big "we've decided to be partners" jump, paid on the spot. A Landmark now needs the two of you to have actually said it to each other.

**People can turn against you now.** Below Stranger there's Disliked, Resentful and Enemy. Treat someone badly and they cool on you a bit at a time. Break the promise your whole relationship rested on and it drops at once, though never past Resentful in one go. Keep it up after that and they'll get to Enemy. A Resentful wife tells you to your face she wants you gone; she doesn't reach for a knife.

**Witnesses count.** Mistreat someone in front of your partner and your partner judges it too. Someone who storms off mid-argument still gets judged for what was said.

**Making up takes a while.** Someone you've hurt can come round, but it's about twice as slow as the fall. Back at zero with someone you used to be close to, they're Estranged, not a stranger.

**Characters get more bio blocks.** With SeverActions 4.3.0, enrolling a character in Relationships includes automatic selection and application of several custom bio blocks based on the character's existing information. Anything you select yourself is left alone. Turn it off with Choose Other Bio Blocks in the plugin settings if you prefer to not use them or to only set them manually.

Block changes land straight away, and Drawn To, Expression, Attachment and Appetite allow only one block each since the options are mutually exclusive within those tabs.

**Re-authoring keeps how someone's changed.** It used to wipe out what they'd drifted into.

The dashboard shows the bad side too, and the background judges no longer read anyone's inventory.

**Relationships' custom bio blocks now auto-populated**
With SeverActions 4.0.1 or newer, everyone enrolled in Relationships automatically have the mod's custom bio blocks selected by the LLM and applied. This adds more character definition that helps the LLM roleplay their unique personalities. User-chosen/removed blocks always take precedence.

**Everyone you talk to gets enrolled in Relationships**
Named people you talk to can join your roster. Guards and other unnamed passers-by aren't. Anyone you remove stays removed. Opt-in feature - turn it on in the plugin settings.

**Dashboard now supports Magelight UI**
If you have SeverActions 4.x, you already have Magelight (can also be obtained standalone via Nexus), and the dashboard uses it when Meridian UI isn't installed. In Skyrim VR it's tried first. Prisma UI is the fallback.

**New API for mod authors**
For other mod authors: a read-only C++ API that lets your SKSE plugin see each bond's tier, track, commitment, and more, with a callback when they change. See `For other mod authors` in the GitHub README.
Dashboard now supports Prisma UI. Meridian UI is still preferred for non-VR users when installed.

**Biggest change since the initial launch!**

Relationships no longer requires or depends on Romantasy. It keeps its own bonds now. If you're upgrading from Relationships 1.x, keep Romantasy installed for your first load: your bonds are brought over once automatically, and after that Romantasy is optional. If you decide to remove Romantasy after that, an optional Romantasy Stub is provided that lets saves that listed it keep loading while disabling its functionality.

**Other changes include:**
- New UI using Meridian UI
- NPCs no longer have to be followers/companions to be enrolled and tracked
- Enroll any NPC via hotkey or UI
- Your hotkeys need setting again - now with SkyrimNet's key picker and a modifier each, under Hotkeys in the plugin's settings in the SkyrimNet UI

Tuned initial relationship seeding to take time spent together into account so experiencing a dense day of activity before initial doesn't over-seed the relationship into more advanced stages. Strangers are truly strangers, no matter how busy you were together.

- **Drunk Behavior → Auto-Take Alcohol: ON** for drinks taken from your inventory. If the toggle is greyed out, enable **Require Alcohol in Inventory** first.
- **Configuration → Auto-Give Food: ON** for food requests. **Auto-Give Max Food Items** controls the transfer limit.


> (*) Previous 0.6.7 was a result of SkyrimNet plugin familiarity growing pain. Sorry for any confusion.
